source.name: City of Houston Solid Waste Management Department

destinations.label: Green recycling cart
destinations.description: City of Houston green curbside cart for clean, empty recyclables.

destinations.label: Black trash cart
destinations.description: City of Houston black curbside cart for non-recyclable household waste.

destinations.label: Special handling required
destinations.description: Take to City of Houston Environmental Service Center or approved drop-off.

destinations.label: Check official guidance
destinations.description: Uncertain item; refer to City of Houston waste directory or 311.

decision.reason: Batteries cause fires in collection trucks and recycling facilities. Never place them in curbside carts.
decision.narration: Batteries require special handling. Take them to a City of Houston Environmental Service Center.

decision.reason: Electronics contain regulated materials and are not accepted in curbside carts.
decision.narration: Electronics cannot go in curbside carts. Take them to an authorized electronics recycling drop-off.

decision.reason: Plastic bags and film tangle in sorting equipment and are strictly prohibited in the green cart.
decision.narration: Plastic bags and film go in the black trash cart because they tangle sorting machinery.

decision.reason: Styrofoam and foam packaging are strictly prohibited in the green curbside recycling cart.
decision.narration: Styrofoam and foam packaging belong in the black trash cart.

decision.reason: Number 6 plastic (polystyrene) is not accepted in Houston curbside recycling.
decision.narration: Plastic marked number 6 belongs in the black trash cart.

decision.reason: Greasy or food-soiled paper and pizza boxes contaminate recycling and must go in the trash.
decision.narration: Food-soiled paper and greasy boxes go in the black trash cart.

decision.reason: Rinsed and drained aluminum and bimetal soup or beverage cans go in the green recycling cart.
decision.narration: Clean metal cans go in the green recycling cart.

decision.reason: Empty and rinsed glass bottles and jars are accepted in the green curbside cart.
decision.narration: Clean glass bottles and jars go in the green recycling cart.

decision.reason: Clean, flattened cardboard boxes go in the green recycling cart.
decision.narration: Flattened cardboard boxes go in the green recycling cart.

decision.reason: Dry, clean newspapers, magazines, catalogs, junk mail, and office paper go in the green cart.
decision.narration: Clean paper goes in the green recycling cart.

decision.reason: Rinsed gable-top and shelf-stable beverage cartons go in the green recycling cart.
decision.narration: Clean beverage cartons go in the green recycling cart.

decision.reason: Clean plastic bottles and jugs marked resin numbers 1 through 5 and 7 go in the green cart.
decision.narration: Clean plastic containers go in the green recycling cart.

decision.reason: Textiles, clothes, shoes, and pillows are not accepted in curbside recycling.
decision.narration: Textiles belong in the black trash cart or a donation bin.

decision.reason: Food scraps and organic waste cannot be sorted in curbside recycling carts.
decision.narration: Food scraps and organic waste go in the black trash cart.

decision.reason: Composite materials made of mixed bonded layers are not explicitly listed in Houston curbside guidelines. Check official city guidance or call 311.
decision.narration: Composite materials require checking official City of Houston guidance.

fallback.reason: No verified City of Houston rule covers this item. Please check official city guidance.
fallback.narration: I am not sure about this item. Please check the City of Houston guidance.
